exercises.name: Wall Push-Up
instructions: Get into the starting position for the Wall Push-Up, hands (or handles) set at shoulder width unless the variation calls for a wider or narrower grip.
Brace your core and keep a straight line from head to heels (or hips, if kneeling/seated).
Lower under control until you feel a stretch through the Chest, keeping elbows tracking over your wrists.
Press back up to the starting position, fully extending without locking out aggressively.
form_cues: Keep shoulder blades pulling down and back, not shrugged toward your ears.
Exhale on the press, inhale on the lowering phase.
Keep wrists stacked under elbows throughout the movement.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike, breaking the straight body line.
Flaring elbows out to 90°, which stresses the shoulder joint.
Rushing the eccentric (lowering) phase instead of controlling it.
safety_notes: Stop the set if you feel sharp or joint pain (as opposed to normal muscular fatigue).
Master the bodyweight/light-load version before adding intensity or load.

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Up
instructions: Set up in the starting position for the Scapular Pull-Up, gripping the bar/handle/dumbbell with a firm, neutral wrist.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades down and together before bending the elbows.
Pull through until your Lats is fully contracted, keeping the movement controlled rather than jerky.
Lower back to a full stretch under control and repeat for the prescribed reps.
form_cues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
Keep the core braced to avoid excessive body swing.
Squeeze at the top of the movement for a full second before lowering.
common_mistakes: Using momentum (kipping) instead of controlled strength.
Not achieving a full range of motion at the bottom.
Rounding the lower back during the pull.
safety_notes: Stop the set if you feel sharp or joint pain (as opposed to normal muscular fatigue).
